chapters.title: Microsoft's naming roulette: lakehouse vs warehouse
OneLake: the data lake you already own
Delta and Parquet: the unsexy heroes

takeaways: In Fabric, a warehouse is the SQL-first home for curated reporting, while a lakehouse is the flexible workbench for semi-structured data and Spark, and both sit on the same OneLake storage.

OneLake stores tables in the open Delta Parquet format, which combines columnar efficiency with ACID transactions, schema enforcement and time travel so SQL and Spark engines can work on the same files.

Shortcuts let teams reference data in other workspaces or external stores without copying it, but because SQL access can run under the shortcut creator's identity, workspace roles, item permissions and shortcut creators need governance.
hook: If your team keeps arguing about lakehouse vs warehouse and copying the same datasets into five places, this episode gives you a plain-English mental model of Microsoft Fabric. Data and BI teams learn what OneLake, Delta Parquet, shortcuts and workspace permissions actually do, so they can cut duplicate storage and get consistent numbers.
